title: Premature JSON Pre-serialization Caching
pattern: Pre-serializing database records or struct fields into JSON strings and caching them in database columns or memory to avoid serialization costs.
why_bad: Pre-serialized JSON prevents database indexing, complicates updates (forcing raw string parsing or rebuilding on every field change), and introduces inconsistency. Modern serialization libraries (like `serde` in Rust) are incredibly fast, taking nanoseconds [299].
detection: Database schemas or memory models containing cached string records of JSON objects alongside raw fields.
counterexample: A static asset pipeline or CMS generating static JSON files that are directly served by web servers without modification. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Store data in structured fields and serialize to JSON on-demand using highly optimized serializers.
